security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by defensive examples, readable Chinese prose, Markdown syntax, SVG paths, and documented installation locations. One high-risk behavior is confirmed: claim-check executes claims-file commands through shell=True, so hostile or insufficiently reviewed input can run arbitrary code. Static review was capped at 400/554 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 154 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The claim checker executes command strings from a claims file through the user's shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace free-form shell commands with structured executable and argument fields plus a strict allowlist. Until then, require an isolated environment without secrets or network access.

content.value_statement: Complex agent tasks often begin before scope, risk, and evidence requirements are clear. This skill adds gates, role discipline, verification, and explicit acceptance.
actual_capabilities: Classifies tasks by risk and defines a pre-implementation confirmation gate.
Surveys installed skills, reusable templates, existing implementations, and reference sources.
Supports single-agent, subagent, and commander coordination modes.
Defines task packages, ownership, trust tiers, evidence records, and closure rules.
Requires fresh verification and marks untested claims as UNVERIFIED.
Provides optional scripts for self-checks, claim checks, probes, and mutation testing.
limitations: It improves execution discipline but does not increase model reasoning capability.
Its primary rules and most supporting documents are Chinese-first.
Full workflows add overhead to small or time-sensitive tasks.
The claim checker executes reviewed commands and is not a security sandbox.

use_cases.title: Structure a complex implementation
use_cases.description: Define scope, risks, resources, verification, and acceptance before changing a codebase.

use_cases.title: Coordinate independent agents
use_cases.description: Assign roles, package tasks, track evidence, and keep one accountable owner.

use_cases.title: Audit completion claims
use_cases.description: Compare stated results with fresh tests, files, screenshots, and explicit coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to assess my task. State the risk tier, needed resources, plan, and verification before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a bounded task

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an evidence plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Define acceptance criteria for this deliverable. List fresh evidence, tested input ranges, and anything that must remain UNVERIFIED.

prompt_templates.title: Run a rigorous implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the full workflow to this high-impact change. Track scope, risks, decisions, review findings, tests, and final acceptance evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate multiple agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a commander workflow for this task. Define roles, task packages, trust tiers, handoffs, evidence requirements, and final DRI closure.

output_examples.input: Add account export to an existing web application.
output: Risk tier: medium because the change handles personal data and affects multiple layers.
Resources: existing export services, privacy rules, test fixtures, and browser tooling.
Acceptance: permission checks, complete exports, cancellation handling, and verified download behavior.

output_examples.input: Review whether a reported migration is complete.
output: The migration claim remains UNVERIFIED until fresh tests and database checks are attached.
The evidence plan covers rollback, record counts, constraints, and representative edge cases.

output_examples.input: Coordinate separate implementation and review agents.
output: One DRI owns closure, while implementation and review roles receive separate task packages.
Each handoff includes scope, prohibited changes, evidence locations, and unresolved risks.

best_practices: Use the light workflow only for specific, reversible, low-impact tasks.
Attach fresh evidence to every completion claim and label untested areas UNVERIFIED.
Keep one DRI accountable even when several agents contribute.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a declared plan as permission to implement.
Do not report test counts without naming the covered and uncovered input ranges.
Do not accept another agent's completion statement without checking its evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill improve model intelligence?
faq.answer: No. It organizes execution, evidence, handoffs, and acceptance around the model's existing abilities.

faq.question: Is it limited to GPT models?
faq.answer: No. The name records its origin, but the workflow supports Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other agents.

faq.question: Must every task use the full workflow?
faq.answer: No. Specific, reversible, low-impact tasks can use the documented light workflow.

faq.question: Can it coordinate multiple agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines optional subagent and commander modes with roles, task packages, handoffs, and closure rules.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The core instructions do not. Optional scripts run only when invoked, and the claim checker executes reviewed commands.

faq.question: What does UNVERIFIED mean?
faq.answer: It marks a result that lacks direct, fresh evidence in the relevant environment.
